new_findings.text: One packet finding closed RR:190 blocker ① 'in STAGE PIXELS' and the other explicitly held the unit question open ('What is NOT closed: the unit-to-stage-px scale factor, which still wants one frame measurement'). The open half is closed, and not from the inventory text — from the input path that consumes the number. MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094 passes the freshly computed slashLength straight into InputManager.setMaxDistance, InputManager.as:106-108 stores it as maxDistance, and :198 loads distanceLeft = maxDistance at mouse-down. The drawn blade path then spends that budget in Euclidean units of the DESCALED stage space: :342-343 compute mouseX/mouseY as (stageMC.mouseX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale, :355 takes the squared distance between consecutive descaled points, and :367 subtracts it from distanceLeft. That coordinate space is the native game stage — :348 bounds it by StatsManager.stageWidth/stageHeight and :231 rejects any release with mouseY > 480, the literal native height. So slashLength is a length in native 800x480 stage pixels by construction, no scale factor outstanding: a 1080p capture is that space times 1080/480 = 2.25 (before pillarbox). No frame measurement is needed, and none should be commissioned.

new_findings.text: RR:158 opens claim 4 with 'In-combat stance is HARD-LOCKED in v0.717 ("CANNOT CHANGE STANCE")', treating the on-screen caption as proof of a lock. The caption is the Focus bar's ZERO-STATE LABEL. Web BattleUI §1t113s0§.as:326-359 is updateReload: it computes _loc3_ = (reload - 48) / (maxreload - 48) clamped at 0, sets the bar scaleX to it, and then drives ONE textfield §1t5169s0§ through three states — _loc3_ == 0 shows the grey §1t5204s0§ (:111, getString(960)), 0 < _loc3_ < 1 hides it, _loc3_ >= 1 shows the black §1t5203s0§ (:110, getString(175) = 'Critical Hit') and plays Snd_criticalDamage. The -48 offset is the same 48 the stance switch costs (§1t99s0§.as:3060, :3162), so the bar reads empty and the caption shows precisely while the switch is unaffordable. I OPENED THE FRAMES AND LOOKED, in both longplays. reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png and reference/frames/combat_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t0445s.png / _t0505s.png (battle, no overworld '+' button) show HP and Chi bars above a third bar that is EMPTY, captioned 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE'. reference/frames/combat_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t0170s.png / _t0530s.png and reference/frames/zFt_combat/zFtCaTO0_1M_t0320s.png (overworld, '+' button and speech bubble visible) show that same slot reading 'HEAVY STANCE' / 'BALANCED STANCE' — the OverworldHUD bust text, getString(645)/(644). Both longplays are early low-level fights, so the meter had not reached 48. THE FRAME AND THE CODE AGREE; the ledger's reading of the frame is what fails. Corroborating detail: getString(960) has no entry in the v0.682 string table (2,533 rows, ids 959/960/961 all absent) and android BattleUI.as:259-263 has no such caption and no -48 offset at all — the two-state caption is a v0.717 web addition, which is why the Android artifacts could not explain the text.

new_findings.text: RR:195 skills-meters blocker ④ is bare: 'SPD->cooldown formula'. RR:90-91 lists 'the SPEED-stat->cooldown formula' as a KNOWN-UNKNOWN, and RR:200 progression blocker ① asks to measure 'SPD range/cooldown scaling ... per-point deltas in a build'. The formula is in web v0.717 source, two functions below the slash-length one. §1t1523s0§.as:2289-2296 is 'if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5;' and its caller applies the same SPD + gear-bonus + x1.5-speed-buff preamble the slash-length getter uses. Android StatsManager.as:1844-1860 names it getSkillCooldownModifier / getSkillCooldownModifierVal, confirming what the obfuscated pair is. So SKILL_COOLDOWN_MULT = 1 - min(SPD_eff, 600)/600 * 0.5, a linear ramp from 1.0 at SPD 0 to a hard floor of 0.5 at SPD 600 — skill cooldowns can be halved and no further. It is displayed to the player as '0.xxx' next to slash distance (web §1t5957s0§.as:3014 getString(983) + int(modifier * 1000); android InventoryUI.as:2233 'skill cooldown modifier: '). BUILD DIVERGENCE: android caps at 300, not 600 — 'if(speed > 300) { speed = 300; } return 1 - speed / 300 * 0.5;' — so the web ramp is half as steep and a v0.717 recreation must take 600.
new_findings.build: web v0.717 (android v0.682 caps at 300 instead of 600)
new_findings.quote: §1t1523s0§.as:2291-2295 'if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5;' ‖ android StatsManager.as:1854-1860 'internal static function getSkillCooldownModifierVal(speed:int) : Number { if(speed > 300) { speed = 300; } return 1 - speed / 300 * 0.5; }'
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters: blocker ④ CLOSES as CONTRACT (web). Config: SKILL_COOLDOWN_MULT = 1 - min(spdEff, 600) / 600 * 0.5, spdEff = STAT_SPEED + gear SPD, x1.5 under BUFF_SPEED. Together with the slash-length formula this also closes the 'SPD range/cooldown scaling' half of RR:200 progression blocker ①, leaving only the DEF mitigation curve there.

new_findings.text: RR:195 skills-meters blocker ③ asks for 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)', RR:190 combat-core blocker ⑤ asks for the 'Focus/crit gating rule' with the close-path 'watch the Focus bar fill/consume', and RR:88-89 lists 'the Focus/crit gating rule (fill trigger/amount/consumption)' as a KNOWN-UNKNOWN. All of it is in web v0.717 source and none of it needs watching. MAX: §1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' = 192, a constant, set at battle init with the meter starting at 0 (:250). new_findings.text: RR:190 combat-core blocker ② is 'crit 1.3 vs 3 final — *read one crit popup.*', and RR:88 repeats it as a KNOWN-UNKNOWN ('crit x1.3 vs x3 final read'). No popup is needed. The web v0.717 damage function settles it in one line: §1t99s0§.as:3274 'return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;' where _loc2_ is the post-stance damage and §1t1243s0§ is the additive crit-damage stat (declared :83, assigned from param6 of initAttackStats at :278, named STAT_CRITICALDMG in android MCSPlayer.as:249/:256). Independently, the inventory stats panel hard-codes the same 1.3 for all three stances when it previews crit damage — §1t5957s0§.as:2727, :2736, :2745 all read '_loc42_ = 1.3;' and :2751-2752 apply it as _loc1_ * _loc42_ + _loc12_. So CRIT_MULT = 1.3 multiplicative plus a flat gear term, on target-build source, and the 'x3' folklore is not a competing reading of the same number. BUILD DIVERGENCE: android is NOT 1.3 — MCSPlayer.as:3215-3222 returns maxDamage * 1.5 in Light and * 1.2 otherwise, so the wiki's flat 1.3 matches the WEB build specifically and any Android-sourced crit number is the wrong build.
